content.text:
The bug is fixed: `tomli.loads('s = "caf\\u00e9"')` now returns `{'s': 'café'}`. The full suite passes (19 tests, 1 skipped).

The cause was in `parse_hex_char` in `src/tomli/_parser.py`. It advanced the position by `hex_len - 1` instead of `hex_len`. That left the parser on the last hex digit, so the digit was read a second time as a plain character. That is where the extra `9` came from. I changed it to `pos += hex_len`, which also covers `\x` and `\U`.

I added a regression test, `test_unicode_escape_does_not_consume_following_chars`, to `tests/test_misc.py`. It checks `\u` and `\U` escapes in basic strings and in a multiline string. I didn't change or remove any existing tests.
